label: M3 S11 | Data Validation, Conditional Formatting & Dashboard Skills

steps: Select the target cell (e.g., B1 for scenario selection)
Click OK — the cell now shows a dropdown arrow
skills.pro_tip: Instead of typing options directly, point the Source to a named range: =ScenarioList. Adding a new scenario to the list automatically updates the dropdown. Create the list on a hidden 'Setup' sheet.

use_cases.connected_function: SWITCH or CHOOSE references this cell
Filters data or changes reference year
IF checks this cell to add/remove line items

skills.key_action: Data → Data Validation → Allow: List → Source: Bull,Base,Bear
Data Validation → Allow: Decimal → Between 0 and 1

common_rules.why: Revenue can't shrink >50% or grow >100% in a year
WACC below 5% or above 20% is likely an error

examples.plain_english: Terminal growth must be less than discount rate

examples.rule: Date must be in the future
examples.plain_english: Maturity date must be after today
Assets = L + E within rounding tolerance

skills.key_action: Data Validation → Allow: Custom → Formula: =AND(B1>0, B1<B2)

skills.guidance: Use Warning, not Stop, for experienced users. In models used by senior analysts or PMs, Warning alerts flag unusual inputs but don't block them — because sometimes a 60% growth rate IS correct (e.g., a startup). Stop alerts are for non-finance users.
skills.input_message: A tooltip that appears when the cell is selected. Shows guidance: 'Enter the revenue growth rate as a decimal (e.g., 0.12 for 12%)'. Set in Data Validation → Input Message tab.

use_cases.reveals: Which companies have the best/worst margins at a glance

skills.key_action: Home → Conditional Formatting → Color Scales → Green-Yellow-Red
Home → Conditional Formatting → Icon Sets → 3 Traffic Lights
skills.customisation: Right-click the icon set → 'Edit Formatting Rule' → change the threshold values. Default thresholds (33%/67%) are almost never useful for financial KPIs.

skills.skill: Custom Formula Rules — The Power Tool

examples.description: Highlight entire row if stock is a BUY
Red text if balance sheet doesn't balance
Bold if company is in the portfolio
Strikethrough if data is > 1 year old

skills.key_action: Conditional Formatting → New Rule → Use a formula
skills.dollar_sign_warning: When you write =$G2="BUY", the $ before G locks the column (always check column G) but the row reference is relative (moves with each row). If you write $G$2, every row checks the same cell. Always test your formula on the first AND last row.

skills.acid_test: Show your dashboard to someone who didn't build it. Don't explain anything. Time how long it takes them to understand the main insight. If it's under 10 seconds, you've built a good dashboard.
skills.definition: A dashboard is a single page that gives the viewer everything they need to make a decision. Culmination of Sessions 9 (Pivot Tables), 10 (Charts), and 11 (Validation + Formatting).

design_rules.meaning: Everything fits on one screen/print page

design_rules.example: Scenario dropdown, year selector, sector filter
design_rules.meaning: Dropdowns and slicers go in the top-left corner
Big numbers across the top row

design_rules.example: Revenue trend line, segment breakdown bar
design_rules.meaning: Visual elements in the middle/centre area
Supporting data at the bottom for drill-down
The viewer should not need to scroll horizontally
